limitations_and_boundaries: The proposed methods should not be viewed as replacements of classical numerical methods (e.g., finite elements, spectral methods) which have matured over 50 years and meet robustness and computational efficiency standards.
The method does not quantify uncertainty associated with neural network predictions, unlike previous Gaussian process approaches.
There is no theoretical guarantee that the L-BFGS optimization converges to a global minimum.
The method's success depends on the PDE being well-posed and having a unique solution, and on sufficient network capacity and collocation points.

experiments_or_tasks: Learn the latent solution u(t,x) of the Burgers equation from Nu=100 randomly distributed initial and boundary data points, using a physics-informed neural network with a 9-layer deep neural network (20 neurons per hidden layer, hyperbolic tangent activation) trained via L-BFGS on the composite loss MSE = MSE_u + MSE_f, where MSE_u enforces initial/boundary data and MSE_f enforces the PDE residual at N_f collocation points.

methods.name: Physics-informed neural network (PINN)
methods.protocol_description: A deep neural network approximates the solution u(t,x). The loss function is MSE = MSE_u + MSE_f, where MSE_u is the mean squared error on initial and boundary data, and MSE_f is the mean squared error of the PDE residual at collocation points. Training uses L-BFGS, a full-batch quasi-Newton optimizer. The network has 9 hidden layers with 20 neurons each and hyperbolic tangent activation, totaling 3021 parameters.
